vid_urls.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Postflight News Conference (Oct. 15, 2026)
vid_urls.description:
After spending over seven months in space, members of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 will discuss their mission aboard the International Space Station during a news conference at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev returned to Earth on Oct. 8, after spending 237 days living and working in orbit. (Adenot will return to Europe and not be available during the news conference.)

Learn more about Crew-12's science and technology research: https://go.nasa.gov/4jdAre7

Watch Crew-12's return to Earth: https://youtube.com/live/x6p9Ri0DlNE

Read more about Crew-12's return and today's event: https://go.nasa.gov/3UikER9

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will answer questions about their mission.

vid_urls.title: U.S. Spacewalk Preview News Conference (Oct. 20, 2026)
vid_urls.description:
We're giving a preview of two upcoming spacewalks on Oct. 29 and Nov. 5 to finish installing solar arrays that will provide more power to the International Space Station. 

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will participate in both spacewalks. The spacewalks will be the 285th and 286th conducted in support of space station assembly, maintenance, and upgrades.

NASA participants in the news conference include:
- Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, Low Earth Orbit Program
- Garrett Hehn, spacewalk flight director, Flight Operations Directorate

Learn more about the spacewalks: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97
Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station

results.name: Artemis Acceleration Press Conference

vid_urls.title: Artemis Acceleration (Oct. 23, 2026)
vid_urls.description:
Tune in as agency leaders provide an update on NASA's plans to return American astronauts to the surface of the Moon by 2028. 

Participants include:
- NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
- NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya
- Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager

As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Moon missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.

More about the Artemis program: https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space...

results.description:
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk will install and deploy the eighth and final IROSA on the 3B channel of the space station, completing the power augmentation upgrades.

The final two roll-out solar arrays will complete the space station’s power system augmentation. Together, the eight roll-out arrays will increase available power by up to 30%, boosting the station’s electric power generation capacity from 160 kilowatts to approximately 215 kilowatts.

info_urls.title: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun
info_urls.description: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun

results.description: Solar Orbiter, a partnership between ESA and NASA, will perform a gravity assist maneuver with Venus on December 24, 2026. Throughout its mission it also makes repeated gravity assist flybys of Venus to get closer to the Sun, and to change its orbital inclination, boosting it out of the ecliptic plane, to get the best – and first – views of the Sun’s poles.
